messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: planned missing design simulation
parts:
Hi,

The problem occurs when the multicore feature is used. The main problem is that the lavaan package is not called in the slave node. The problem can be simply solved by not using the multicore feature for now. We will fix this bug in the next version.

Just a note that the scale of your analysis model has not been identified. Adding std.lv=TRUE in the sim function might be helpful.

Best,
Sunthud

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: planned missing design simulation
parts:
Hi ya,

The lavaan package calculates starting values by pairwise deletion. The problem of using planned missing data design is that some pairs of variables may not have any values of missing.

After you run the script, you will see the error if you run the following scripts:

dat <- generate(popModel, n = 500, empirical=TRUE)
dat <- impose(miss.model, dat)
out <- sem(analyzeModel, dat, start=out)

I still cannot find a good solution for you. I try to impose starting values in the sem function using the 'start' argument but lavaan is still unable to get through the calculating pairwise correlation. I also analyze the data by parameter table and impose starting values manually. This approach does not work too. If I know more, I will let you know.

Best,
Sunthud

On 04.08.2013 08:51, Sunthud Pornprasertmanit wrote:

Hi ya,

The lavaan package calculates starting values by pairwise deletion. The problem of using planned missing data design is that some pairs of variables may not have any values of missing.

After you run the script, you will see the error if you run the following scripts:

dat <- generate(popModel, n = 500, empirical=TRUE)
dat <- impose(miss.model, dat)
out <- sem(analyzeModel, dat, start=out)

I still cannot find a good solution for you. I try to impose starting values in the sem function using the 'start' argument but lavaan is still unable to get through the calculating pairwise correlation. I also analyze the data by parameter table and impose starting values manually. This approach does not work too. If I know more, I will let you know.

Best,
Sunthud

Hi,

The problem occurs when the multicore feature is used. The main problem is that the lavaan package is not called in the slave node. The problem can be simply solved by not using the multicore feature for now. We will fix this bug in the next version.

f1~~1*f1;f2~~1*f2;f3~~1*f3;f4~~1*f4;
f3+f4~f1+f2
"

However, the same error as before happened with the new code. Hopefully this change could help solve this issue to some extent.

I have one further question, is there any simple way to specify the starting values? The way in the above situation feels a little bit repeat.

Best regards,

ya
